title: Windows x86_64 production unsafe baseline and host-selected ratchet baseline

criteria: the complete release gate measures each host against its own reviewed unsafe baseline: unsafe-default.json for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, unsafe-default-<host>.json otherwise, with no fallback when a host has none

the Windows baseline was produced by unsafe_ratchet --write-baseline (held v0.21.51 build, scanner 5d7c4203fa2a) from the Linux baseline's historical inventory, matched scans of f397a911f and e1e283463, and a 69-component review

35 reviews were ported only where every reviewed file re-hashes to identical bytes; 15 Linux-scoped reviews were rewritten after inspecting the Windows code; 19 Windows-only crates were reviewed from source, each with a stated residual limitation
unsafe_ratchet gate mode on the e1e283463 Windows measurement is clean: 378 packages, 397 files, no unreviewed exposures

the http-transport serve_once fixture reads the whole request (head and Content-Length body) before replying, so a POST body sent in a later segment is never left unread when the socket closes (Windows resets such a socket and the client loses the reply with os error 10054)
